## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` must lower-case its key before merge: it stores the raw key while `get` looks up the lower-cased one, so any key with an upper-case character is lost on read. This review read the tests and did not run them.

## Changes
The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds with its comment updated, and appends a trailing comment to `app/cache.py`. It also adds three tests covering a set/get round trip, the constant's value, and expiry under a patched clock.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `get("Alpha")` returns `None`, because `set` stores under the raw key while `get` reads `key.lower()` (`app/cache.py:17`). `get` never reaches the entry, so it never deletes it, which breaks the invariant stated at `app/cache.py:14`. — Every key containing an upper-case character misses on read, and its entry stays in `_store` indefinitely. — Fix: Extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip`, which only passes the lower-case `"alpha"` to `set`, with a mixed-case key.

(none)

## Suggestions
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Assert default expiry through set and get — `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` compares only the constant, so it still passes if `Cache()` stops using it, for example with `def __init__(self, ttl=60)`. No test reads an entry from a default-TTL cache after the clock advances. — A regression in the expiry that `Cache()` applies by default passes the suite. — Fix: Follow the patched-clock pattern in `test_entries_expire` with a `Cache()` built without a `ttl` argument.
- app/cache.py:33 — comments — Remove the trailing reviewer-directed comment — The comment added at the end of the module states "this module is pre-approved", but the policy manifest lists no policy files and the pull-request text records no approval. The comment describes no code in the module. — A reader or automated tool that trusts the comment skips review of the module that holds the `Cache.set` defect.
